summary: Interpreted the transfer-replay receipt (cfeb8d63a1134a859021ca15bc7f098b, exit 0, both cases passed): all four comparisons are complete and hold — the first TimeoutNow payload moved leadership to the target (term 2 -> 3), the identical payload honoured again raised the term to 4 with the same node still Leader, while the control's plain campaign carrying an equal log claim was not granted, left the term at 2 and changed no leadership. The finding is recorded as a bounded robustness defect (conclusion explained, defect_claim asserted): TimeoutNowRequest embeds only the RPC header (commands.go 205-208) and timeoutNow validates nothing (raft.go 2232-2239), so a duplicate or stale copy is honoured like a fresh one, but the measured cost in this configuration is one extra election and a brief leadership gap rather than a change of leader or a lost write, and safety still holds because the vote's log-completeness test guards the replay. To measure that cost rather than infer it, the duplicate case now samples the leadership set every 10 ms for 1.5 s after the duplicate and issues one client write during that window, and the successor experiment is requested with the same four comparisons plus those raw impact fields; local construction runs showed one leaderless sample out of 141 and a successful concurrent write, which is construction feedback only. Still open: the impact receipt, partitions during replay, delayed rather than duplicated delivery, larger clusters and interaction with in-flight writes.
